::: {.callout-warning}
## Draft guidance

The Lab Book is a living resource. Draft pages and proposed policy require review; they do not establish approved laboratory policy.
:::

Welcome to the **GeoEpi Lab Book**, a shared place for practices that help geographical epidemiology remain understandable, defensible, reproducible, and transferable across people, projects, and time.

## Find your next step

- [Start a project](start/new-project.qmd) for a minimum setup and scope.
- [Assess project readiness](templates/project-readiness-checklist.md) at lifecycle checkpoints.
- [Document incoming data](templates/data-source-inventory-template.csv) with a source inventory.
- [Find a template](templates/index.qmd) for reusable project records.
- [Prepare a handoff](templates/project-handoff-template.md) before responsibility changes.
- [Review the minimum standard](start/minimum-standard.qmd) for the proposed baseline.
- [Research Practices](practices/index.qmd) for the lifecycle from planning through preservation.
- [Domain Guidance](domains/index.qmd) for spatial, epidemiological, ecological, genomic, and modeling topics.
- [Lab Standards](standards/index.qmd) for future lab-level decisions.
- [Templates](templates/index.qmd) for reusable project and documentation structures.
- [Resources](resources/index.qmd) for an annotated external catalog.

The intended outcome is that a lab member can join a project, understand what was done and why, reproduce an important result where access permits, identify uncertainty, and continue the work without relying on undocumented memory.
